req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for subsequent DELETE calls on the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-028 requires DELETE /tasks/{task_id} to be idempotent: the first call on an existing task returns HTTP 204, and every subsequent call on the same task_id returns HTTP 404. The test suite covers: (1) positive/STC — the full state transition from existing→deleted→gone, asserting exact status codes 204 then 404; (2) negative/NEG — deleting a task_id that never existed returns 404 immediately; (3) boundary/BVA — deleting a newly-created task (id=21, the first id beyond the pre-loaded 20) then re-deleting it to confirm 404; (4) DT — a decision-table test covering all three branches: pre-existing task first delete (204), second delete (404), and a never-existing id (404), asserting the exact detail message text to catch string-mutation operators; (5) STC — three consecutive DELETE calls on the same id to confirm the 404 is stable across multiple retries, not just the second call.

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_existing_task_state_transition
preconditions: Task with id=5 exists in the pre-loaded dataset (title='Write project report', completed=false)
Database is reset to 20 pre-loaded rows before this test
actions: Send DELETE /tasks/5 — first call on an existing task
Assert response status is exactly 204
Send DELETE /tasks/5 — second call on the now-deleted task
Assert response status is exactly 404
Assert response JSON detail contains the task id
expected: First DELETE returns HTTP 204 with no body
trace: Catches status-code mutation (204→200, 404→200) and boolean-flip in crud.delete_task
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_existing_task_state_transition():
    r1 = client.delete("/tasks/5")
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    assert r1.content == b""

    r2 = client.delete("/tasks/5")
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert "detail" in body2
    assert "5" in body2["detail"]

tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_newly_created_task_boundary_id():
    rc = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "BVA boundary task", "completed": False})
    assert rc.status_code == 201
    created = rc.json()
    task_id = created["id"]
    assert task_id == 21

    r1 = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    assert r1.content == b""

    r2 = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert "detail" in body2
    assert str(task_id) in body2["detail"]

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_three_consecutive_calls_stable_404
preconditions: Task with id=3 exists in the pre-loaded dataset (title='Submit expense report', completed=true)
Database is reset to 20 pre-loaded rows before this test
actions: DELETE /tasks/3 — call 1 → expect 204
DELETE /tasks/3 — call 2 → expect 404
DELETE /tasks/3 — call 3 → expect 404 (stability check)
Verify GET /tasks/3 also returns 404 confirming permanent deletion
expected: Call 3: HTTP 404, detail mentions id 3 (idempotent across multiple retries)
GET /tasks/3: HTTP 404 confirming task is gone
trace: R-TASK-028: idempotency must hold for N>2 subsequent calls, not just the second

tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_three_consecutive_calls_stable_404():
    r1 = client.delete("/tasks/3")
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    assert r1.content == b""

    r2 = client.delete("/tasks/3")
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    assert r2.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 3 not found"

    r3 = client.delete("/tasks/3")
    assert r3.status_code == 404
    assert r3.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 3 not found"

    rg = client.get("/tasks/3")
    assert rg.status_code == 404
    assert rg.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 3 not found"
